exposure: surgical findings (volvulus, meconium pseudocyst, jejunoileal atresia, malrotation-malfixation anomaly, volvulus due to internal hernia, Meckel's diverticulum, gastroschisis, perforated appendicitis, anal atresia, gastric perforation)
cohort: Newborn patients (n=41) who were followed up and treated for intrauterine gastrointestinal perforation in a pediatric surgery clinic between December 2009 and 2021.
finding: Higher total intubation time, earlier first stool passage postoperatively, and ileal perforation were significantly associated with mortality, while jejunoileal atresia was less frequent in deceased patients.
